content.title: 2026 Valero Texas Open money: Here’s how much every player made
content.text: With wet and windy conditions all weekend in San Antonio, the PGA Tour’s final pre-Masters tournament had players battling the elements before heading to Augusta, Georgia. Robert MacIntyre and Ludvig Åberg entered Sunday at the Valero Texas Open atop the leaderboard, but Matt Wallace, J.J. Spaun, Andrew Putnam and others quickly clogged the leaderboard at TPC San Antonio. Wallace fired a final-round 68 to take the clubhouse lead at 16-under par, but then had to sit around for two hours to see if that would be good enough for his first PGA Tour win since the 2023 Corales Puntacana Championship. But Spaun birdied the par-3 16th and then eagled the short par-4 17th to get to 17 under and take the clubhouse lead. Spaun had to finish his third round to start Sunday and played his final 27 holes 9-under to grab the lead. He then watched as Michael Kim, Putnam and MacIntyre all failed to match his number, giving him his third-career win and second victory at the Valero Texas Open.
